codes.sample: 207 medical students (56.0% male), three public universities in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia; cross-sectional online survey, 20 May–15 June 2026 (232 responded, 25 excluded).
codes.ai_system: AI tools in general for study (mostly Gemini 45.9% and ChatGPT 41.1%)
codes.dependence_measures: 9-item subset of the AI Dependence Scale (AIDep-22; Wu et al.), covering cognitive dependence, functional dependence and loss of control; 5-point Likert; mean score; α = 0.837, ω = 0.940. Modelled as one latent factor. Mean 2.83 (SD 0.78).
codes.note: Correlates: academic self-efficacy (GASE-5), depression (PHQ-4 items). Only SEM paths adjusted for gender, age, year, daily AI use: dependency→ASE β=0.298; →depression direct 0.608, total 0.545 (Table 2). No correlation matrix. Supplement (S1 loadings, S2 covariates) not described as having correlations. Could ask the author for data.
